questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to explore other cultures

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, they where very helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing was provided through the university, and I would really recommend Global Village to any person attending Osaka University. It is very clean, and they staff were so sweet and helpful with anything

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was about a 10 min bike ride and 20 min walk to get to the nearest campus. From Global Village the nearest train station (Yamada St.) is a 5 min walk, so the transport-options to/from campus was not a hurdle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Well, if you chose to do your study abroad in Japan, you must prepare yourself to do a lot of paperwork. I was frustrated at times, but when I think back on it now, it was only really frustrating in the moment. We are lucky, that we live in 2025 and that google translate exist (a translator app was often a must when doing paper-stuff at the City Hall)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot - specially the staff at the dorm (Global Village)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull! I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was much lower than the level at KU. Although the level was lover, the workload was higher - so it reminded me a lot of being in high school.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any lecture while studying in Japan. The teaching-style varies a lot, and it depends a lot on which course you are taking. Mostly the teaching-style consisted of the teacher doing a lacture-talk in class, but much more relaxed than a lecture at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalization Studies 
Japan: Society and Ideology
Self-formation throughout life
Ethics and Criminology
Critical Thinking in A Global Context: Navigating the Challenges Ahead (SS)
Ethical and Regenerative Cities
Japanese Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend the course 'Ethical and Regenerative Cities'. The teacher was so nice and really had some cool and exciting guest-lectures to come join the class as well. 

For at true Japanese experience, I would recommend 'Japan: Society and Ideology'. The teacher is from Japan himself, and it is a true experience to get his perspective on a lot of things.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to bear in mind, that it is mandatory to sing up for the national pension and national health insurance in Japan. You would get a discount, because you are a student with no income, but you are automatically signed up - and there is no way around that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is so cheap, but fruit and vegetables are more on the expensive side. A lot of the times it was actually cheaper to eat out than cooking yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of student activities were offered - there is a club/circle for literally anything at the uni that you can join I did not though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to the north of Japan, and the south of Japan. Also, Kyoto is only a 1 h train ride from Osaka.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Japanese people are so polite, so after af few weeks you catch yourself bowing and saying thank you at the supermarket as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Be quiet in the train!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness for sure! But also the food culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for paperwork :) But do no hesitate, this exchange was one of the best things I have ever done!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hmm, no I do not think so. If any, the uni gives you too much information about everything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The people from DK that I missed greatly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
